disposition_reason: Seventeen elements including As, Cd, Pb and Ni were measured by ICP-OES in 12 samples each of sheep milk, whey and fresh cheese from one farm in a heavily disturbed mining area of eastern Slovakia; Table 2 gives mean ± SD and median.

study.design: Single-farm monitoring, biweekly sampling of milk, whey and cheese over one lactation, with risk scenarios
study.origin: one ecological sheep farm (about 450 ewes) in the Spiš region, eastern Slovakia, a heavily disturbed area from long-term mining and industry

period.as_reported: every two weeks from April to late September (year not stated)

study.qa: Method verified with certified reference materials (ERM BD151, BB184, BCR 274) and internal standards; recoveries not printed

controls.control: processing milk into fresh cheese vs whey
controls.comparator: raw sheep milk from the same farm
controls.outcome: Pb mean 0.04 (milk) -> 0.13 (cheese) and 0.09 mg/kg (whey); As 0.46 -> 0.73 (cheese) and 0.24 mg/kg (whey); Ni 0.09 -> 0.70 mg/kg in cheese

unresolved: Se values are below the stated Se LOD (2.0 mg/kg); flagged.
Arsenic means (0.24-0.73 mg/kg) are high for milk products measured by ICP-OES; not resolvable from the text.
Cheese was also made with additional milk mixed during preparation (Methods), so cheese is not purely from the study farm.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: EU maximum level for lead in milk (EC Regulation 1881/2006, as cited)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: 0.020 mg/kg; exceeded by mean Pb in milk, whey and cheese
